subject: [RFC PATCH 2/5] mm: add a_ops->dirty_folio_range() and use the mkclean dirty harvest

2026-09-03.patch_summary: This patch adds two new operations to the Linux kernel: `a_ops->dirty_folio_range()` and `folio_mark_dirty_range()`. These operations allow a filesystem to mark only specific ranges of a folio as dirty, rather than the entire folio. The patch also updates the `folio_clear_dirty_for_io()` function to use these new operations instead of marking the whole folio dirty. This change is intended to improve performance by reducing unnecessary writes and allowing filesystems to track dirty state more accurately.

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that folio_mark_dirty() clears PG_reclaim, but mapping_dirty_range() does not, and requested the latter also clear PG_reclaim.
reviews.raw_body:
folio_mark_dirty() clears PG_reclaim, but mapping_dirty_range() doesnt.
Do you need to clear PG_reclaim here?

2026-09-09.patch_summary: This patch adds a new operation to the address_space_operations structure called dirty_folio_range(), which allows filesystems to mark specific ranges of a folio as dirty instead of the entire folio. It also introduces a new function folio_mark_dirty_range() that uses this new operation. The patch then updates the folio_clear_dirty_for_io() function to use folio_mkclean_dirtymap() and hand the dirty ranges to the filesystem, reducing unnecessary writes in cases where only part of a folio is modified.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a concern about redundant code in folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_dirty_range(), agreed to fix it by moving the clearing into mapping_dirty_range() in v2, which will be folded into the next version of the patch.
